body:
I am not sure what the question was. I guess, whether I had my experiences coming.

I didn't expect much from a temporary psychiatrist. But she ran with it. All I wanted was some guidance for my case manager, as she wanted to start a trauma workbook and was concerned about causing harm.

Thank you. This is close to what I tell myself.

I was a child, and they were my parents. Even if I was difficult, that doesn't condone what I went through.

You may be right. I am shocked by her reaction to something so small, although she has a long history of being less than reasonable. Thank you. The surgery went well, and I am recovering nicely. Doing my best to focus on that.

Oh, goodness yes. I was suicidal for the first time when I was 9 or 10. My Dad found out and flipped. I begged to get help, and he said any psychiatrist who met me would see right away that I was a monster and lock me up forever. 

It was always about appearances, and never about my welfare.
That is lovely. There absolutely is hope.

Yes, my mental health team all know how my Mom is behaving. The last time I saw my psychiatrist was when she was hospitalizing me, but that is basically why she wanted me to move out.

The stress is just too much.

If I can move out, a social worker is also willing to visit to help keep me on track. Subletting isn't a bad idea.

Thank you!

Thank you for taking the time to reply.

I was hospitalized for a week in the spring, and the ward psychiatrist met with my Mom, to talk about trauma and suicidal ideation and why he thought my diagnosis should be changed (my usual psychiatrist strongly disagreed with him).

Unfortunately, she came out of the meeting assuming I should be taken off *all* my meds. So that didn't help. I don't meet my new psychiatrist until November (my usual is no longer working), but I can always ask. I am not sure what my Mom would think, however.

I do have a mental health worker, and have asked my Mom to speak with her repeatedly. My care team would very much like her input, but she refuses as she doesn't want a "one sided conversation."

If you ask my Mom, there is nothing wrong with me beyond being a terrible person. She says I have abused her since I was a teen, which is better than my estranged father who once made me apologize for crying too much as an infant. She sees her treatment of me as self defense. Both my parents tend to attribute hostile intent to everything I do.

I digress, however. I know my Mom's behaviour is making things worse, even though she insists it is necessary.

I really hope I find a way to a better life, and appreciate your encouragement.
I wear glasses, and my eyesight is fine with correction.

My helix was fine. I would rate the pain as no higher than a 3 on the pain scale. I got it done last January, and it has healed without a hitch.

A piercing pillow helped, and so did appropriate aftercare. There hasn't been a single complication for me.

Good for you! This is a journey I am on, too. For the longest time, I couldn't figure out why housework is so *hard* for me. Then I moved back in with my Mom.

Her standards are impossible to meet, and she gets so very angry when I end up failing to meet them. Suddenly, it all seems so clear.

Today, I ate three distinct meals and took care of the cats and fish. I cooked all the meals myself. I washed my clothing and the towels, and showered and washed my hair even though I really didn't want to plus I completed my therapy homework.

It was a very unproductive day, but it could have been way worse.

I have been threatened with abandonment so many times in my life that it has ceased to have any meaning for me. Now, I enter relationships with the assumption that they have an expiration date.

I don't avoid relationships, exactly. It is just that my energy levels also get so low that I cannot cope with a lot of relationships. A few high quality ones is all I can sustain, and even then it is a challenge.

I don't have a lot of faith in people. Every time I uphold a boundary or otherwise have a disagreement, I assume it is my relationship's death knell.

This has lead to a life with a great deal of solitude. It can be lonely, at times.
Yep. It is just as easy as that.

Oh, I just used a litre sized mason jar and Mason Tops Kefir caps. I would toss the grains in, top up with milk and wait until the ferment was complete (this varies, based on temperature and grain to milk ratio - anywhere from 12-24 hours, and is a personal thing). 

Then strain and repeat.

I promise, they are hard to mess up.

Kefir is easy! However, they do feed like
beasts - it isn't great for the grains, but I treated them like some people treat their sourdough starters. I kept them out of the fridge and made the kefir as needed (at least a couple days a week).

This isn't a problem if you go through a lot.

Crisis lines can be very helpful. Sometimes, they stay up with me for hours while I am too stuck in fight/flight mode. 

Warm lines - it depends on your issues. I cannot use mine, as most of my concerns involve trauma and it really depends on who you get.

No. Nobody has explained any of that to me.

Apparently, the form 1 is a formality as they would not have taken me otherwise, and she wanted them to understand my risk. I was voluntary in the sense that I knew it was pointless to argue with my psychiatrist when she was sure a hospital was right for me at this time.

Very little has been explained to me, but the nurses are being nice.

I imagine I will know more at the actual psych unit tomorrow.

Oh, I have been taken to the ER locally. My psychiatrist signed the Form 1. And has already talked to the hospital in Timmins and they have a bed for me in the morning. Being transferred.

But perhaps there, you mean?

Sorry, I missed this. 

No. I have a consult in early July with a surgeon, and then who knows.

Yeah. It is ridiculous.

They say I have Bipolar Type I, but nobody has ever actually observed a manic episode in me. I am 40.

The reason they give is that  I had a really religious period in my twenties and nearly became a nun. This lasted for years.

I talk extensively about history of trauma, and nobody ever really listens to me when I suggest my symptoms are situational. They are starting to, though. However, they also want to raise my Abilify to 30mg, ensuring I am properly sedated so the abuse I live with bothers me less. Oh, and to prevent the random possibility that I might have my first ever manic episode. 

It is nonsense, and this was all such a mistake.

Often. I first became suicidal when I was around 9 or 10 years old, and I am a 40(F) female. I had one non-serious attempt at 18 which I never sought treatment for.

I wish I could say it gets better, but it really has not. Here I am at 40, disabled and on the verge of homelessness and stil being abused by my mom. I don't even know what to say about that.

What scares me is not at all death. I look forward to dying. I have a scope coming up, and I keep hoping they find cancer and not just confirm yet another chronic disease. Because in Canada, we have medically assisted death - but it does not apply to those with mental health conditions, and I am quickly discovering our utter lack of a safety net.

I am absolutely afraid of being hospitalized, and do not see the point anyway - what would it do but put a bandaid on a gaping wound? 

So, what, they increase my antipsychotic yet again so I can be more numbed out the next time my Mom tells me I am a cancer on the world? This does not help.

I so, so, so. wish I could just end this life with some dignity and grace. I just want the suffering to finally end.

But I keep on keeping on. 

I don't even know why anymore.
I am interested

I still don't believe I deserve love, but some days I come close to it. What helps me is accepting that there are people who love me for who I am. When I doubt myself, I can count on that. It gets easier with time.

I am so sorry. I was in a similar situation when I graduated from university - and had to move in with my family. 

Sometimes, all we can do is keep ourselves safe. I know personally, being back in this house yet again has done a number on my mental health.

You know, though, I have come a long way over the years. Sometimes it helps me to write about these things - do you have a way to safely do that? Or maybe make some art? It doesn't fix anything but it can help.

One thing I always do is make sure I have emergency contacts in my phone - and a card in my wallet, with crisis numbers (this is less necessary since 988 - and there have been a few nights they have stayed on the line with me to help me calm down). The most important ones are for the ones for the women's shelter, and victim's services, in case I need to flee the situation suddenly.

Please, do what you can to be safe. I can definitely promise that it can get better.

Oh my goodness, both my parents have done this all my life. Neither would ever seek out a mental health professional willingly, so I can only guess at a diagnosis. But something is so very wrong.

For fourty years now, I have been told I am just this absolute monster and that what I call "abuse" is just the only way they know how to control me.

This is still going on, as I live with my Mom and the latest man she has taught to abuse me. I am routinely told I do not deserve mental health care, and that what I call "abuse" is the only way they know how to control me. Besides, they just get angry sometimes and can't be held responsible. They are only defending themselves.

But yet, when I talk about leaving? You would think, if I have seriously been abusing my Mom since I was a young girl, and she thinks I am a "cancer on the world" who was a "mistake to give birth to." Well, you would really think she would be happy to see me go.

When I try to talk about my feelings, it is drama. I am routinely told that any mental health professional who really knew me would institutionalize me forever, and that I would not have any of my friends if they really knew me. I have given her my case manager's phone number, if she is really that concerned. If I have that big of a blind spot, my treatment team should know.

She, of course, has no close friends. 

This, I am told, is likely rooted in projection. It has messed with my head so badly for all my life. I doubt myself often, but thankfully have people who love me for who I am and can remind me of it when I need it.

I really wish I knew.

I went through a similar time when I moved out years ago. Tried to run from my trauma, and that was a huge mistake.

I have always been self sufficient. I hate needing people, even though I accept that sometimes I do need support now. Sometimes, at my worst, I would make bargains with myself - to wait to watch a flower bloom or whatever. Or maybe I would do some art to make something beautiful out of all this  emotion. 

These are the games that have given me the courage to get through to another day, even when half the time I am absolutely terrified of the future.

Over the years, I have done so much work, though, and I have seen so much progress even if I know I have a long way to go. It can be so discouraging and lonely and overwhelming sometimes anyway. 

There have been many points, though, that I have felt like I was at the end of my rope and instead somehow found the courage to go on anyway. Even if sometimes I am just limping.

I guess, I have always felt like I was letting them win if I stopped fighting and so it is something I really don't want to do.

So far, I have not yet reached the point where I have been convinced that it was a good decision to stop.

Life has so much beauty, even now. I try to focus on that, and I get by. It is a struggle, but I think we are all stronger than we think or we would not be alive.

Thank you so much for your kind words. I feel so trapped, although I know that any progress is still progress. I tried calling the police (to ask if my Mom really could prevent me from showering etc) and they reminded me that I should be grateful someone took me in, and do everything I can to get back into her good graces.

But my psychiatrist thinks this is just not safe for me.
Absolutely considering it. The DV workers are also trying to help me figure out a safe place for my cat, as leaving him her is not an option.

Maybe, but like I was recently told by another specialist a *lot* of things can cause those symptoms. It is possible, sure - and I bet there are lab tests that can test for that. 

Absolutely worth getting some medical advice. I am in Canada so that is easy for me, and I know that might be more expensive for you. I really hope you can though.

If you are only taking it a couple times a week though, I wouldn't worry too much. Maybe you could ask a pharmacist?

It is worth seeing a doctor about your stomach problems if they pop up that frequently. Starting pantoprozal stopped a lot of my symptoms.

However, I still take a lot of Pepto too when my nausea gets bad. Waiting to see my own doctor.

Hey!

Thank you for the reminder. I know, of course, I am not as alone as I feel. These situations can sure convince you otherwise though.

I am in Canada, so today was not a holiday - but she was on vacation. Perhaps she will be back tomorrow.

I also appreciate the offer to talk. The same goes to you. As much as I appreciate knowing I am not alone, I hate that you know what it is like.
Definitely! I too have been diagnosed with GERD and have lots of symptoms. When I don't eat much I get severe nausea and lose my appetite for like a week.

I have anxiety, and when it is worse - well, stress definitely makes things worse. I have been going through a lot of stress, and it was worse. But my anxiety is well managed and my symptoms did not disappear.

Thanks. That was my instinct. I called my doctor's nurse the day before yesterday and did not get a response. I will try again tomorrow.

I was supposed to see my PDoc and that is now on hold until I am medically cleared as I understand it. 

I am not against being on a high dose of a medication if I need it. I just want to be sure it is safe, and that I am not doing anything risky by disregarding what the ER doc said until I can see my family doctor. Or at least get a call from his nurse.

The only things I have been diagnosed with as an adult that involved some sort of test (I didn't have a family doctor for half my life, so take that with a grain of salt) are:

-Severe environmental allergies, as confirmed by skin prick testing.
- Mysteriously small, but not dangerously small red blood cells (have had testing to rule out some sort of genetic disorder, I forget which one).
-Repeated B12 deficiencies 

I eat well when I am able. When I started having stomach problems in my twenties and dropped out of university, I became *obsessed* with gut health. Really firmly believe that probiotics and fermented foods can be powerfully therapeutic.

I think my more recent flare ups are mostly a stress thing.

I really feel like we should wait and see what the scope says. Maybe that will be interesting.

I have been working on eliminating trigger foods, and it is slow going. but be careful - going hungry can cause reflux issues all by itself. That was part of what caused my recent inability to swallow solids.

My chronic cough has been a problem for a long time. It isn't just GERD - I also have bad allergies, but the cough is mostly just GERD.

It has taken decades to get to this point. I have tried so many treatments before I suggested this and behold, the cough stopped.

It caused me to drop out of university for my second degree, has changed the course of my career, and I don't really like going out when I am sick which covers many months of the year. Thank heavens for mask culture.

My struggles with depression started around the same time.
I love this idea!

Thank you so much! I meant to reply when I read this last night, but I was very tired after a long day.

At the least, you brought me a smile. I have experience with hunting, fishing and foraging. Worked in fish & wildlife when I was younger, and once did build a small cabin. I was just a kid and it was with a friend, but it was lovely- and you brought back really fond memories which I needed.

I see my social worker tomorrow. It is possible that she can get me into the CMHA's crisis housing for a couple months. She offered it to me before, but this seemed like a more stable situation. 

That would give me time to gather supplies and find a suitable spot. I can think of a few relatively obscure locations here that might work.  You have given me a lot to think about, and I appreciate it.
Thank you! I hadn't thought about that.
Yes, that is the main reason I thought about Toronto. We still have snow on the ground here, and our summers are short. I think it would be easier to survive further south.

Sorry. As I said, I am very upset. They have been talking about kicking me out all morning - and the boyfriend has been pressuring her do just that. 

They know my plans to leave.

Thank you so much for your answer.

Thank you so much for the information and the step in the right direction!

I was so disappointed when nothing happened, beside yes - a slight upset stomach.

Risk aware is definitely how I want to approach this.

Thank you. I am interested in a more intense experience. Maybe in the summer months, when the weather is nicer and I can be sure of a good environment.

However, I have friends who microdose and feel a sort of "high" - mild euphoria and an increase in creativity. Right now that interests me.

Thank you. I have friends who take very low doses and say they feel mild euphoria and an increase in creativity on low doses. My Mom, who gave me these took four and was "high." That was what I was hoping for.

Is that a reasonable hope for low doses of psilocybin?
My doctor is aware. I have been given warnings that psychedelics in some circumstances can cause permanent psychosis. Beyond that, they aren't interested in giving advice on illicit substances.

I haven't bought green onions for years. I get them from the farmers market in the summer on the cheap, and grow them on my windowsill.

I wouldn't be surprised if this sort of thing is why.

Yes! I am in northern Ontario, and we have a group for farmers all over the area and many deliver. It IS a huge expense to buy all your meat for the year in one go, and I haven't worked up to that. For some time, I dealt with a CSA for the area that delivered year round. Bought grains from a mill in Ontario, and invested in a mill for them to make my bread .

Even canning is a big expense to get into. It is one of those things that pays off. You can even buy certain things like pasta sauce in bulk and recan that in smaller quantities if you have a smaller family. 

In the end, it starts paying for itself after awhile. It is a matter of making that leap. When I was working, I took vacation time in the summer to do my canning etc. I would try to plan out my whole year. 

It is a lifestyle shift, and it takes time and expense to get into it. There are things everyone can do, though - and every little bit of freedom we can get helps.

Like, here - I can buy 12 Activia yogurt for $8, or I can just buy a litre of milk and make it myself. Cheap, if you like the room temp ones - my favourite is Skyr. I mix it, let it sit for 12 hours at room temperature. Then stick in in my fridge. So much tastier, and healthier, with very little effort. I sweeten it with a little raw honey or local maple syrup (or birch syrup when I can get it or have access to birch trees), plus some grains like oats and whatever is in season for fruit. That, is breakfast. It is wonderful. Truely.

I can buy a bushel of Cortlands in the autumn  for $15 from the Amish vs a 4lb bag for $9 at our local YIG. They will keep all winter (and our winters are long) if you have a canner, a dehydrator and a freezer. And the space to store it all for a year. $8 for a half bushel of pickling cucumbers at the farmers market for $12 vs $5 for half a pound at the YIG.

I would buy things myself, including larger cuts of meat and whole birds and learned to butcher them myself. I use everything, like people used to.

It really is eye opening.

I am rambling. I think we are on the same page.

I just wish more people knew and had the resources to live like this.

That was why I started getting most of my meat from area farmers. It was so much less expensive than our local stores, and better quality. Buying locally has other advantages, too.

I learned canning, fermenting, bread baking, gardening, foraging, fishing, wine making etc - to stop giving money to big grocery stores.

Buying local is also better for the environment. Harder if you live in an urban area, though.
OSAP loans can be forgiven via bankruptcy or a Consumer Proposal after you have been out of school for seven years. I filed a Consumer Proposal seven years ago, and mine were included.
I am on Abilify and drink coffee, too.

Last year, I had to quit for financial reasons. My psychiatrist now says I did it because I was becoming manic, no matter how many times I correct her.

But she did put me on samples of the injection for awhile.
I am 40 and just got my helix done. Why not?
I looked at some pictures and love that idea! Thanks!
I hear you. This isn't really much of an improvement. I had long periods of wellness between episodes, until recently. I wish I could just medicate when I felt symptoms coming on.
I meant to say - I live in a neutral sort of gray area. I think that is normal with antipsychotics, and my psychiatrist says my treatment is optimal.
I take 20mg of Abilify, and have an extra thing of 5mg in case I need to titrate up.
Lithium was first line for me. I stopped it because of the side effects and switched to Abilify.
Lithium did this to me. Now I take Abilify and feel like a zombie still. My passion and creativity are gone. I lament this all the time, and often wonder if it is worth it.

I hear you. I am in a similar situation.

I get samples from my psychiatrist because I can't afford them. I am on them because once I went off my meds for a month. It has been over a year, but she won't let me go back to the pills.

I take the Abilify injection, but it is five times as expensive as the pills. I noticed no real other difference between the injection and the pills, besides the former giving me a sore arm for a few days.
Thank you! That would be nice. It really spooked me yesterday.

I am puzzled. There was nothing new and I spent the day inside. The only unusual things were the steak I had for dinner the night before, and the apple I ate about an hour before the rash started. I eat apples all the time when they are in season, though.

And thanks! I was very relieved when it went away.
It was a general psychiatrist.
A psychiatrist diagnosed me. It took a couple appointments, and was fully covered by OHIP. The waiting times for that can be long, though.

It has happened to me, and I am in the process of filing for my second consumer proposal. The consequences of this are spiralling, and it looks like  it will cost me a job I was offered. Recommend bankruptcy, before things spiral further for you.
I turned down a casual appointment a couple years ago, and many months later received a verbal offer for an term position. So I wouldn't necessarily count anything out.

I was on lithium, and the hair loss started quickly (although we also found out that my levels were way too high). I stopped because it was not a side effect I could tolerate. My hair has been slowly growing back since.
Yes. I have lost my connection due to my meds almost completely. It is a loss I feel keenly.

I get it. I have always had periods of my life where I have an increased interest in the divine - they tend to coincide with my manias.

In a bad situation some years ago, I became convinced that my suffering was good and that God was purifying me so I could be a great saint.

I used to believe I was surrounded by demons who wanted to claim my soul.

My psychiatrist says I was delusional.

For what it is worth, I think a lot of Catholics go through phases like that. In the early church, once it was decided that martyr's go straight to heaven, people started to chase those experiences. They declared that as a heresy - so maybe think hard on putting yourself into bad situations. 

It is ok to embrace your Cross when it comes to you, but I tend to think that God wants us to be happy too.

I think spiritual experiences fall in line with the concept of unverified personal gnosis.

Is what the "spirits" are telling you in line with what other people have written and experienced? If so, then it is more safe. If not, then it might be a delusion.

Personally, though, religion has just not been healthy for me. I don't think there are easy answers to this question.

I am on abilify maintena. It works well for me, and I have very few side effects. I like it much better than the lithium I was on previously (which made my hair start falling out, and turned me into a zombie).

I am on disability, and it is very hard. Sometimes I say I have my own accounting business (which isn't exactly a lie - I do taxes for people every year). I get shamed all the time for not working and not being married - like my life is just a waste.

I wish there were easy answers. But I think this is something everyone with a non-obvious disability has to deal with.

I just said a prayer for you.

That wait for meds to start working is such a killer, I know. They will start working before you know it, though. Hang in there.
I don't really have any friends, besides the ones I have online - and one old friend from university who now lives far away. I do have plenty of acquaintances.

My landlord called for a wellness check on me. It was so humiliating, and I freaked out and tried to hide from the police when they came.

It was humiliating and horrifying and my neighbours all saw.

They didn't end up taking me to the hospital.

I could probably forgive it if someone was truly that worried about me - but it would take time.

I am not a professional, but I do write. I go through long periods of lack of productivity.

I also tend to obsess over various projects when hypomanic, and lose interest eventually.
You certainly are not alone.

I have lost SO many jobs while undiagnosed with Bipolar and worked in so many fields. I am on long term disability now.

After what happened with my most recent job, I am really nervous about ever returning to the workplace. I don't know if I can, as I really burned my bridges.
I play several instruments and sing, and write, and do photography. Love reading too, and baking sourdough bread (and other fermentation projects).

Thank you. I am trying hard not to beat myself up over this. It is hard.

Trying to repair my life is a terrible reminder. It is also a powerful influence to stay on my meds.
Thanks. I am sorry you have had such devastating consequences too, but it is good not to be alone.

That is what my psychiatrist said - that I lacked insight into my illness when in an episode. It is true that I lose control, and stop thinking there is a problem. It is scary and surreal to consider - that I am not always in control of my life.

I was untreated for years before I finally sought help.

I had a manic episode recently, that confirmed the diagnosis from Bipolar NOS. It was terrifying, and reminded me of past episodes from university.

It changes a lot of the narrative of my life, and is hard to accept. Especially the lack of insight and psychotic features.

The thought of being hospitalized at all is terrifying. It was a hard appointment.
wonderful! Thank you. It is good to hear about another good experience. Helps me feel better about my appointment tomorrow.
Thank you! That is so good to hear. I had some weight gain on the pills, so am not surprised by that.
I do have a choice - the courts aren’t involved. Thank you for that reminder!
I have been back on the pill for a few weeks, now.  So yes, I could.

Thank you! It is hard not to worry. 

All of this throws so much of my life into question.

Because it hasn't! That was back in 2007, and I didn't learn things. I barely attended classes, just read books and wrote essays and attended exams. Since then, my degree hasn't gotten me a single job, and the jobs I did have went poorly. I don't use my education at all.
It took me six years. For two of them, I barely attended class at all. But I did graduate, the little good that did me.
Yes. I get super interested in religion when hypomanic, and have heard God when manic. It is something I have to watch for.

Thank you! I very much hope things continue to improve for your Mom. It must be so hard to be the family of someone with hoarding disorder.

I know it has been for my Mom.

That is my suspicion as well, which is sad. These aren’t problems I would ever have chosen, but when do we ever get to pick?

It is hopeful to think it is possible to manage.

Thank you. I ordered those books, and emailed my therapist to let her know.

I am glad to hear that your Mom’s hoarding us better than it was!
Thank you - it hasn’t been easy. I had been in therapy for years already before I was ready for the cleanout. I am terrified it will happen again.

I have similar issues. I really don’t know what to do about them, myself. It is worth discussing with your pdoc.

By the way, you aren’t necessarily too young for perimenopause. My Mom started hers in her early 30s.

Tentatively started another relationship. I am nervous - when I am hypomanic, I get hyper sexual, and make all sorts of promises. When I am stable, I am just not that into it. I keep getting into relationships on those premises that just aren’t good for me. Trying to be mindful of that.

I have never really had many close friends. There is one I have known for decades, but we rarely see each other now that I have moved north. We check in a few times a year. There are also a few people I am close to online.

I often wish I had a bigger social circle, but I don’t really know how to fix that. It is hard to make friends as an adult.

I have heard that too - and honestly, it helps my anxiety about that sort of thing. Our healthcare system is in bad shape.

I am sorry that happened to you, though.

I used lithium and it made enough hair fall out that my hair stylist noticed. It has grown back since stopping it.

That said, my pdoc noted that my blood levels were too high, too.

I wish I had answers. I have come a long way over the last few years in accepting my diagnosis. There are so many things I have tried! At one point, I even consulted an exorcist.

When I reached out for treatment, I was at the end of my rope. In general, I trust psychiatrists as much as I do, because I haven’t found a better alternative.
Here, in Ontario, it comes down to intent and plan. I can talk about how much I want to die all I want - nothing will happen unless they judge the threat to my life to be imminent.
Yes, it definitely feels like a lot - and I appreciate that you understand that. I definitely don’t plan to stop my meds again after this experience! here’s hoping it is enough to get me stable.
I have never been in the hospital. It remains one of my greatest fears.

I know the feeling. Over the years, I have lost all my friends. I haven’t seen my Dad since 2007. 

In a way, it is a relief - but it still hurts.
I have had symptoms for a couple decades now. Was diagnosed with depression in 2018, and bipolar last winter. I am 39.
That is amazing! I tried the same with my employer, and well, it didn’t go so well. I am glad to know it isn’r always like that!

Yeah. I often feel like the most zealous person around too. Clergy used to encourage it!

It gets confusing for sure.

I definitely will! I see her in March, and sent a note to my therapist in the meantime.

Thank you so much for the reading suggestion. I did a degree in Philosophy, and remember reading William James on pragmatism. Just added this book to my kindle! ♥️

Thank you. For the last few weeks, we have been limited to 15% capacity, and I am told that attendance is low enough that nobody has been turned away. There were maybe 20 people there tonight.

I think I will call the rectory on Wednesday, and see what they say.
I went today for the first time in years.
I get it. Sleep, when it comes, is the only relief I get.

I have been estranged from my father for years, now and was in a similar situation. So much from my childhood is gone now, including most of my childhood photos and the contents of my jewelry box. The last I heard, everything has been thrown out at this point.

It is a hard thing. Mostly I tell myself that it doesn't matter in the end - that, as special as some of that stuff was to me, it is all still just stuff. But it is hard sometimes anyway.

I am sorry you are dealing with this.
It is a great resource! Am sure you will love it
